memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "Judah got a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar. But Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the LORD's sight; so the LORD put him to death" - Gen 38:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah arranges a marriage for his firstborn, Er, to a woman named Tamar. But then comes a stark and sobering statement: "Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the LORD's sight; so the LORD put him to death." The Bible does not even tell us the specifics of Er's wickedness — but God saw it clearly, and God acted.

This is a hard verse, and it confronts us with a truth we do not always like to face: God is holy, and He sees what is hidden in the human heart. Er may have appeared fine to those around him; his sin is not described for us. But "the LORD looks at the heart" (1 Sam 16:7), and nothing is hidden from Him. What people overlooked, God saw.

We live in an age that often imagines God is indifferent to how we live, or that private sin does not really matter. This verse quietly reminds us otherwise. God is not mocked; He sees, He knows, and He is just. Sin is serious to a holy God.

Yet even this sobering truth is meant to lead us not to despair but to reverence and to grace. Because God sees our hearts, we cannot hide from Him — but we also do not need to. We can come to Him honestly, confessing our sin, and find that "if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us" (1 John 1:9). The God who sees is also the God who saves those who turn to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do you live as though God sees your heart, not just your outward actions?
Where do you need to take sin more seriously before a holy God?
Are you coming to God honestly, or trying to hide?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Lord, You see what is hidden in every heart, including mine. Give me a reverence for Your holiness, and draw me to confess my sin honestly, trusting Your faithful mercy. Amen.
